narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

A high of 32°C (90°F) and a low of 20°C (68°F) are expected today and tonight, with thunder possible, peaking overnight. Early Partly cloudy conditions will give way to Mostly clear skies by midday, becoming Mostly cloudy into the evening. Wind will be north-northeasterly overnight, turning south-southwest by midday and southwest into the evening, with peak gusts reaching 36 km/h (19 kt). The peak UV index will reach 8.9 today. Air quality reports from ground stations show an AQI of 137 at Kisumu Airport, 66 at Ochieng' Avenue, Kisumu Central, and 61 at Dunga Beach. As of 06:01, reports through 05:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 24°C (75°F); low so far 21°C (70°F); peak sustained 15 km/h (8 kt); sky mostly clear.

## Extended Outlook

NEXT THREE DAYS. Sunday will be Partly cloudy, Monday Mostly cloudy, Tuesday Partly cloudy, Wednesday Mostly clear, Thursday Mostly cloudy, Friday Mostly cloudy, Saturday Mostly cloudy. Models show Sunday dry with 0 % chance, Monday dry with 0 % chance, Tuesday dry with 30 % chance, and a rain chance of 60 % on Saturday. Highs range from 31°C (88°F) to 34°C (93°F) across the period. Record notes: Day+0 best rain record ECMWF, right 87 % of the last 30 checks.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Thunderstorms are possible overhead, peaking at 23:00. Model convective energy peaks at 540 J/kg for GFS, 2600 J/kg for ECMWF, 540 J/kg for ICON, 1960 J/kg for UKMO, and 2840 J/kg for Best Match, placing Best Match, ECMWF, and UKMO above the thunderstorm threshold. Any thunderstorm brings the hazard of sudden gusts well above the forecast wind. No warning has been issued by the met service.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Winds over Winam Gulf will run overnight at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting 11 km/h (6 kt), then south-southwesterly by midday at 6 km/h (3 kt) gusting 16 km/h (9 kt), then west-southwesterly into the evening at 16 km/h (9 kt) gusting 26 km/h (14 kt); peak gust 29 km/h (16 kt). Where thunderstorms are possible, sudden gusts well above the forecast wind remain a hazard.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1009 hPa) and highest toward the northeast (1016 hPa) — a 7 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the north is deepening over the next three days. Pressure is also falling toward the east, northeast, northwest, south, southeast, southwest — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is falling. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across 5 points, today's mean sea-level pressure sits between 1012.4 and 1015.0 hPa; falling by 1.6 hPa over three days. Overhead pressure trend is +0.6 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others here yet, though ECMWF holds the best rain record across Day+0, Day+3, and Day+7. Today's call of 32°C (90°F) high and 20°C (68°F) low sits alongside GFS at 32°C (90°F)/19.2°C (66.6°F), ECMWF at 31.5°C (88.7°F)/20.2°C (68.4°F), ICON at 31.5°C (88.7°F)/20.9°C (69.6°F), UKMO at 31.5°C (88.7°F)/18.5°C (65.3°F), and Best Match at 32°C (90°F)/21.2°C (70.2°F). GFS does not see this location's thunderstorms coming, while ECMWF systematically under-forecasts peak wind despite calling for 30.6 km/h (17 kt). Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) predicts a max of 31.0°C (87.8°F) and min of 20.0°C (68.0°F), agreeing with the call. Data sufficiency shows a settled picture with 75 checks at Day+0, 40 at Day+3, and 97 at Day+7, though KMD has fewer checks than the other models. Best Match duplicates ECMWF rain probabilities.

extended_outlook:
Temperatures and winds much the same through Tuesday, with thunderstorms likely each day. Skies partly cloudy throughout. Tuesday's call: dry, 30%, with one of four models wet; highs around 33°C (92°F). Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) calls it dry. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 90% of the time over 101 checks.

Further out, cooling through Saturday, with thunderstorms likely Wednesday, showers and thunderstorms likely Thursday, and showers and thunderstorms possible Friday and Saturday. Wednesday: one of four models wet, highs around 33°C (91°F). Thursday: three of four models wet, the week's wettest day at 4 mm (0.15 in) on average, highs 30 to 33°C (87 to 91°F). Friday: one of three models wet, highs 29 to 32°C (84 to 89°F), thunder possible rather than likely.

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Thursday. GFS, ECMWF and ICON are the wetter solutions from Wednesday to Thursday; UKMO keeps it drier. Saturday's call: rain, 60%, with one of two models wet; highs 28 to 32°C (83 to 90°F). At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 90% of the time over 97 checks.
